utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-29-A, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Appearances, please. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. JARVIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Michelle Jarvis appearing for the Prosecution, together with Ms. Helen Brady, and our case manager today, Mr. Sebastiaan van Hooydonk. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Jarvis. Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. On behalf of General Galic, attorney-at-law Mara Pilipovic, and Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Galic, can you understand me, please? Mr. Galic, can you understand me? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I understand you crystal clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Galic. You may be seated. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was held on the 2nd of November, 2005. I would like to ask you now, Mr. Galic, whether you have any issues that you would like to raise at this time. Do you have any concerns regarding your mental or physical well-being? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have spoken about a number of health issues ever since my arrest. I didn't even realise that I had been indicted, and all of a sudden I was arrested. This was an act of terror carried out against me, although I was not resisting. I was forced into a car, and I received a number of serious injuries on that occasion. I have been suffering from a number of serious health problems since. It was based on that that my Defence filed a request for me to receive treatment in the Republika Srpska or some place like that where the conditions for my treatment would be far better than they are in the Detention Unit. I must say, yet again, that the conditions in the Detention Unit do not preclude treatment, as such, but conditions could improve; that much is certain. There should be better treatment. I was banned from leaving for treatment there, and there was a doctor who examined me here, I believe on the 16th of May, who told me that there was nothing else for me to do but to keep on suffering and try to cope with it. I have problems with my back; that's what accounts for most of my health problems. The other problems are not that apparent for the time being. These are the fundamental things that I wanted to share with you. I wanted to remind you. You know that best of all because you were there right at the beginning when the first decisions were made, and I would not like to tire you anymore with this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Galic. I'm sorry to hear that you still have problems with your back, and I will ask the Registrar to inquire with the Detention Unit whether -- about the state of medical treatment that is now given Mr. Galic and whether anything additional can be done to meet his concerns. Thank you, Mr. Galic. You may be seated. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I believe that there are no outstanding motions in this case. The parties' submissions on the respective appeals from the trial judgement are now complete. The Appeals Chamber hopes that fairly soon it will be able to schedule oral arguments on the merits of the appeals. Before concluding the Status Conference, I want to ask counsel for the Prosecution and for the Defence whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Ms. Jarvis?

utterances.speaker: MS. JARVIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There are no issues from the Prosecution, as such. We would just briefly take this opportunity to update the Court regarding the Prosecution's compliance with its ongoing disclosure obligations. Since the last Status Conference, we have made a number of disclosures to the Defence as documents have come to our attention, and recently the Prosecution has also carried out another periodic electronic search of material which is not already available to the Defence on the EDS. So we were in the process of finalising the reviews from that search. The Defence have been notified by a letter yesterday regarding the procedure for this, and we anticipate that we will be complete with that process within the next couple of weeks. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Jarvis. Any comments of the Defence on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Chairman. First of all -- thank you for giving me the floor. Every time that we wish to speak, this was a problem always before, every time that we take the microphone it's always under reserve concerning our pending motion. We -- as you know the -- we always have to treat it carefully when it comes to impeaching. We are now examining this motion that we have received this morning. This is going to be a fourth point, but the third point is: We should be able to organise ourselves very, very quickly, very soon, and we would like to know whether you, your Chamber, or anybody else could tell us what we should do. If the hearing is taking place, we would like to know how long it would take. And also regarding the length of the trial, that would also be wonderful if we could find out. We were very -- we were advised there was going to be nothing in the month of April. I will then prepare my agenda already now, and this is why I have to tell you that I will not be able to be present in the month of April. And last point, I would like to say this courteously with regards to your Chamber, it could happen, it is not certain yet, but it could happen that I must -- that I will eventually have to withdraw my services from this matter. It could happen, but it is not yet happening. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would your colleague's withdrawal from the case affect your readiness for hearing the arguments on the appeal?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have just been informed, and it's only now that I know about this. I will certainly be notifying the Chamber about any decision taken by my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me say that I will be very concerned if anything happens which can delay the hearing of the appeal of Mr. Galic. I think he has been waiting long enough, and we are really moving forward, the Appeals Chamber, the Bench, rapidly towards being ready to hear the arguments. I take note that Mr. Piletta-Zanin would not be available during the month of April. This probably would not be a problem, but I do hope that problems will not arise which go beyond the limited issue of the month of April. As regards the Prosecution, I'm -- I appreciate your continuing compliance with your disclosure obligation. And again, I hope that the lateness of these additional disclosures would not affect our timetable. I'm anxious to move on with the case and would not -- really would be upset about any delays.

utterances.speaker: MS. JARVIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just raise one additional thing which is related to the scheduling of this matter for hearing. We'd hoped to have an opportunity to discuss this with my friend before the Status Conference this morning. We certainly hope to take it up with them afterwards. But it has been the Prosecution's practice in recent cases to request from the Chamber in advance of the hearing a list of questions that the Appeals Chamber would most like to be addressed on by the parties so that we can all organise our preparations and provide as much assistance as we can to the Chamber. And certainly, the Prosecution anticipates filing a motion along those lines in this case as well to try and organise our work that way, and we will speak to my friend as well and see if we can organise a joint approach on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me understand -- see whether I understand. The motion would be aimed at asking the Bench to give you in advance key questions that we would be asking?

utterances.speaker: MS. JARVIS
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. That's how it has worked in a number of recent appeals, and it would be just for the Appeals Chamber to indicate to the parties the issues or questions that they are most -- would be most assisted being addressed during the hearing. And of course it would be of greatest assistance to the parties in their preparation if we could have that sometime in advance, preferably about four weeks, if that would be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I would be perfectly comfortable with a motion or motions on this matter. It is -- has become increasingly the practice of the Appeals Chamber that even without any motions on the part of the Prosecution or the Defence, we do that. If you look at the Scheduling Orders we issued for the last appeals we heard at Arusha, you will see that they contain questions or areas on which we wanted to benefit from particular attention and focus by the parties. So I don't think this is a major problem, but I take note of your interest in that, and again you are -- you are welcome to present a motion. I'm not sure that, strictly speaking, it's necessary, but no problem, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have consulted my colleague, Ms. Pilipovic, and we have just discovered that this is one of the rare issues with which we are in agreement with the Prosecution. We hope that there will be many more of these agreements with the Prosecution during the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad to hear that, and I certainly share your hope. So I believe that there are no other issues for the parties to raise today. I see there are no other issues, and therefore it remains for me simply to thank the parties for their attendance and their participation, and I will call these proceedings to a close. Thank you.
